title: Boundary wall maximum length, R30-R40 all other lots (65% of the lot boundary)
text: C3.4.4 Boundary walls may be built in accordance with Table 3.4c provided: i. boundary walls are located behind the street setback; ii. overshadowing does not exceed the limits of C3.9.1; and iii. they are finished to an equivalent standard to the rest of the development, to the satisfaction of the decision-maker. Table 3.4c Lot boundary setbacks, R30 - R40 all other lots: maximum boundary wall height 3.5m; maximum boundary wall length 65% of the lot boundary; number of boundaries All; related figure 3.4i.

parts.label: access not from a rear right-of-way

exceptions.label: abuts an existing or simultaneously constructed wall of similar or greater dimension (C3.4.5)

replaces.note: two-thirds of the balance behind the setback, two boundaries -> 65% of the whole boundary, all boundaries

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 3 - Grouped Dwellings.pdf

notes: Applies to R30-R40 lots that are not narrow laneway lots (frontage over 8.5 m or access not from a rear ROW). Walls on all boundaries, so no count rule. Figure 3.4i (p36) applies 65% per boundary and groups W3, W4 and W5 against boundary C, i.e. cumulatively per boundary (register ch3-064); the fact is the longest single wall as % of its boundary, so several walls on one boundary are under-tested.

verified.note: Per boundary and cumulative on the Chapter 3 page: Figure 3.4i (p36) labels W1 against 65% of boundary A, W2 against B, and 'W3, W4 & W5' together against 65% of boundary C. The encoded fact (building.boundary_walls.max_pct_of_boundary, longest single wall) does not capture several walls on one boundary.
